newsitem.title: LATVIA: ESTONIAN MICROLINK PLANS RIGA COMPUTER PLANT.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIAN MICROLINK PLANS RIGA COMPUTER PLANT.

text.p: Estonian computer company Microlink plans to open an assembly plant in Riga in a joint venture with partners, the Diena newspaper reported on Monday.
The initial Microlink investment in the plant will be worth $100,000 and the Latvian side would have to contribute additional funds and credits, the newspaper said.
The planned capacity of the plant is 500-600 units a month, using mainly Intel, Keytronic and ATI produced parts, Mikrolink's marketing manager Peter Mark is quoted as saying.
Microlink has some 15 percent of the Baltic computer market and since 1995 the company has sold units, worth 76 million kroons in Latvia and 53 million kroons in Lithuania, Diena said.
The company also plans its own assembly plant with a similar capacity in Lithuania, where Microlink operates through a rep-office.
Microlink, active also in the west of Russia and some European countries, plans to sell 17,000 units in 1997 and 25,000 in 1998.
